title: Construct a proof, then check the quotient idea

objectives.description: Construct a proof that every maximal ideal is prime.
Recognize the quotient characterization of maximality.

sources.citation: Original proof practice prepared for the Axiora design fixture.
sources.rights: No third-party text reproduced; distribution license not yet selected.

setup.content_md: A maximal ideal has a quotient that is a field; a prime ideal has a quotient that is an integral domain. Build the implication by connecting these characterizations.

construct.prompt_md: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity and let $M$ be a maximal ideal. Prove that $M$ is prime.

hints.content_md: Translate both ideal properties into statements about $R/M$.
A field is an integral domain. Apply the quotient characterization of primality.

construct.model_solution_md: Since $M$ is maximal, $R/M$ is a field. Every field is an integral domain, so $R/M$ is an integral domain. The quotient characterization of primality then shows that $M$ is prime.

rubric.criterion_md: Use maximality to identify $R/M$ as a field.
Explain that a field is an integral domain.
Apply the quotient characterization and state the conclusion.

fresh-check.prompt_md: Which quotient condition characterizes maximality of a proper ideal $M$?

options.text_md: $R/M$ is an integral domain, with no further condition.

feedback.correct_md: Correct. The field characterization is the step that gives the implication.
feedback.incorrect_md: An integral-domain quotient characterizes primality; maximality corresponds to a field quotient.

finish.summary_md: The proof attempt and fresh check are recorded separately. Self-review does not establish machine-verified correctness.
